thread:
Alex Kim: RFC idea — use deterministic Merkle sampling to compress audit logs for BYOK tenants while preserving an immutable proof-of-origin. reduces storage and keeps a verifiable chain for legal/SOC2 audits. thoughts?
Maya Patel: interesting. must prove custody w/ customer-managed keys. how do we tie the merkle root -> KMS signing without leaking keys? :thinking_face:
Dan O'Neill: we can store merkle roots signed with a service-wrap key that is itself encrypted under tenant CMK (BYOK). vault the wrapped key metadata. when customer rotates CMK, we rewrap.
Leo Zhang: product Q: will auditors accept a sampled set + proofs? need to validate with a pilot customer or a compliance partner. also: retention windows + legal hold need to be exact — sampling can't remove evidence during hold.
Sarah Gomez: implementation note: sampling should be deterministic per-tenant/time-window so proofs are reproducible. propose slices per-day -> build merkle tree over events in that slice. sample factor configurable per-tenant.
Maya Patel: agree. also need nonce/salt per-tenant per-window to prevent cross-tenant correlation. salt derived via HKDF using tenant id and window id, but we MUST ensure salt isn't customer secret.
Alex Kim: minimal API surface: POST /audit/proof-query {tenant_id, window_id, event_ids[]} -> returns events + proof path + signed_root_meta. Signed root meta = {root_hash, signed_by:service_key_id, wrap_token_id, window_id}.
Dan O'Neill: quick sketch of signing: service signs root_hash -> signature stored. wrapped_service_key encrypted with tenant CMK via KMS encrypt. store wrap_token_id as pointer. when verifying, we provide wrapped key metadata so auditor can request unwrap via customer KMS (with customer's consent).
Leo Zhang: launch criteria (business): 1) SOC2 audit partner confirms receipts of proofs acceptable, 2) one pilot bank completes end-to-end verification, 3) docs + SDK for auditor verification.
Sarah Gomez: perf tradeoffs: building merkle per-window adds CPU at ingest flush time, but sampling reduces long-term storage/IO. need a batching window (e.g., 10m or 1d) choice tradeoff.
Maya Patel: legal hold flow: if a hold exists for any event in a window, we must retain full un-sampled raw events for that window. fallback policy: pause sampling and mark window as "retain-complete" in metadata.
Alex Kim: edge-case: reingestion/late-arrival events for a closed window — we must publish a new merkle root version and sign it, with incremental versioning. auditors must be able to see history of root versions.
Dan O'Neill: ops: storage schema -> one object per window per-tenant: {events_blob OR sampled_index, merkle_roots[version], signed_root_meta, retention_flags}. Keep size small.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist reminder: runbook for rollback + explanation for oncall. See https://runbook.internal/audit-sampling (stub). :robot_face:
Leo Zhang: risks: auditors could reject sampling; fallback is keeping cold archive of raw full logs for a longer window — cost estimate needed. I'll prep cost delta for 1/3/12 month cold archive options.
Maya Patel: compliance ask: need attestation that wrapped service key access is audited and that we can provide key-usage logs. tie into KMS audit trails.
Sarah Gomez: dev tasks: 1) merkle lib + deterministic iterator, 2) ingestion flush hook + windowing, 3) sample index format + proof generation, 4) signing + wrap/unwrap orchestration. estimate: 6-8 wks for MVP infra + 2-3 wks for SDK + docs.
Dan O'Neill: ops tasks: rotate plan for service key, backup of wrap tokens, inability-to-unwrap runbook (if customer CMK lost).
Alex Kim: acceptance criteria for product MVP (concise): - Proof generation for windows produces verifiable signed root - BYOK wrap/unwrap metadata included in export - Legal hold switches to full retention per-window - Pilot customer verified end-to-end + audit partner signoff - Docs + SDK for auditor verification
Leo Zhang: OK. next steps: Maya to coordinate compliance partner intro, Dan + Sarah to prototype merkle signing flow, I'll coordinate pilot outreach and cost analysis.
Maya Patel: I'll ping our SOC2 auditor and schedule a 30m sync next week.
Sarah Gomez: starting a branch+PR template with a small reference implementation (Go lib + python verifier).
Dan O'Neill: taking prototype card, will timestamp initial spike by EOW.
Alex Kim: thanks all — moving this to a short RFC doc after the sync. :thumbsup:
